label: PF Backlog 475
title: Defect/RCCA: core.backlog.update() must validate structured field types fail-closed (analysis str corrupts item + crashes index write)
body:
Source: defect observed while delivering BI-0211 (2026-10-08).

What happened: ``core.backlog.update(scope, project, eid, analysis="<a string>")`` accepted the string, wrote
it into the item file, then crashed in ``_write_indexes`` -> ``_index_row`` (``(it.get("analysis") or {}).get``
-> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'). Net: a CORRUPTED item (analysis=str) was left on disk
and committed, and the open/closed indexes were not regenerated.

Why it matters: any caller (agent/tooling) can pass a wrong-typed field and silently corrupt backlog state
(fail-open), then a later index write crashes (or, worse, if the field were not read, it would pass silently).

Fix (proper, not a shortcut): in ``core/backlog.update`` (and ``add_epic``) validate known structured fields
before writing - ``analysis`` and ``dashboard_impact`` must be dict|null, ``links``/``decisions``/``deps`` must
be list/dict of the expected shape - and raise a clear ``ValueError`` (fail-closed) WITHOUT writing, so a bad
call can never mutate the store. 5-Why + a new guard (RCCA).

Acceptance: passing ``analysis="x"`` raises ValueError and leaves the item byte-identical; a guard test.

links.backend_capability: module:core/backlog.py, test:test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_backlog_field_types.py

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/agent_structure.py, core/artifact_registry.py, core/backlog.py, core/backlog_link.py

dashboard_impact.reason: internal backlog-store robustness; no dashboard surface
